mainEntity.name: Do I need permits for a room addition in Denver or nearby cities?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most room additions in the Denver metro area need permits, and the exact package depends on the scope of work. New homes and additions typically require zoning, building, and sewer use/drainage permits, and many projects also need trade permits for electrical, plumbing, mechanical, roofing, or siding work. If your addition is close to a property line or changes the home’s footprint, extra survey or documentation may also be required. Preparing the right documents upfront usually speeds review and reduces back-and-forth with the city. A contractor familiar with local permitting can help organize the plans and permit set before submission.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes—most additions need permits, and Denver commonly requires zoning, building, and drainage-related approvals plus trade permits. The exact requirements depend on size, location on the lot, and what systems are being added.
